Name: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
Key_Provisions: Foundational legally binding global treaty on climate change. Objective: stabilise GHG concentrations to prevent dangerous anthropogenic interference with the climate system. Establishes principles including common but differentiated responsibilities. Requires parties to submit National Communications and Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs). Basis for all subsequent climate negotiations and agreements including Kyoto Protocol and Paris Agreement.
UK_Ratification: Ratified 1993; UK bound by all amendments
UK_Links: [LEG-001] Climate Change Act 2008; UK NDC (2035: −81% vs 1990); [LEG-003] Carbon Budget Orders (1st–7th); Net Zero Strategy / Carbon Budget Delivery Plan (CBDP) 2023

Name: Kyoto Protocol to the UNFCCC
Key_Provisions: First legally binding international agreement with quantified GHG emission reduction commitments for developed countries. Established emissions trading, clean development mechanism (CDM) and joint implementation. Committed Annex I countries to ~5% reduction vs 1990 in first commitment period (2008–12); second period (2013–20). Superseded in ambition by Paris Agreement but remains in force.
Parent_Convention: [INT-L-001] UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
UK_Links: [LEG-001] Climate Change Act 2008; [LEG-003] Carbon Budget Orders (1st–7th)

Name: Paris Agreement
Key_Provisions: Landmark legally binding international agreement on climate change. Goal: limit global temperature rise to well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels, pursuing 1.5°C. Each country submits NDCs (Nationally Determined Contributions). 5-yearly ratchet mechanism (Global Stocktake). Article 6 creates international carbon markets. Article 7 establishes global adaptation goal. Loss and Damage (Article 8). Replaces Kyoto Protocol as main mechanism for developed countries from 2020.
Parent_Convention: [INT-L-001] UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
UK_Ratification: Ratified 2016; UK NDC: −81% by 2035 vs 1990 (submitted Feb 2025)
UK_Links: [LEG-001] Climate Change Act 2008; [LEG-003] Carbon Budget Orders (1st–7th); [POL-004] UK Net Zero Strategy / Carbon Budget Delivery Plan (CBDP) 2023; Paris Agreement / UK NDC (2035: −81% vs 1990)

Name: UN Convention on Biological Diversity
Key_Provisions: Internationally binding treaty with three objectives: (1) conservation of biological diversity; (2) sustainable use of its components; (3) fair and equitable sharing of benefits from genetic resources (ABS). Requires National Biodiversity Strategies and Action Plans (NBSAPs). Underpins CITES, Cartagena Protocol, Nagoya Protocol and Kunming-Montreal GBF. Secretariat administered by UNEP.
UK_Links: [POL-003] UK National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; [LEG-004] Environment Act 2021; [ORG-004] Joint Nature Conservation Committee (JNCC); [ORG-005] Natural England; [LEG-010] Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction Act 2026; UN Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) / Kunming-Montreal GBF

Name: Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety
Key_Provisions: Legally binding protocol under the CBD on safe handling, transport and use of Living Modified Organisms (LMOs) resulting from biotechnology. Establishes Advance Informed Agreement (AIA) procedure, precautionary approach to LMO trade. Includes Biosafety Clearing-House information sharing system.
UK_Links: [ORG-020] Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA); [LEG-004] Environment Act 2021

Name: Nagoya Protocol on Access and Benefit-Sharing
Key_Provisions: Supplementary agreement to the CBD providing transparent legal framework for access to genetic resources and sharing of benefits arising from their use. Requires prior informed consent and mutually agreed terms. Includes an Access and Benefit-sharing Clearing-House. Directly relevant to traditional knowledge and CBD Article 15/8j obligations.
UK_Links: [ORG-019] Royal Botanic Gardens Kew (RBG Kew); [ORG-020] Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA); [POL-003] UK National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025

Name: Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework
Key_Provisions: Landmark decision adopted at CBD COP15 (Dec 2022). Sets 4 goals and 23 action targets for 2030 to halt and reverse biodiversity loss. Key targets: 30×30 (protect 30% of land and sea by 2030), restore 30% of degraded ecosystems, reduce harmful subsidies by $500bn/year, mobilise $200bn/year for biodiversity. Includes a monitoring framework with headline, component and complementary indicators. Requires updated NBSAPs from all parties.
UK_Ratification: CBD party; UK NBSAP submitted Feb 2025
UK_Links: [POL-003] UK National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; [ORG-004] Joint Nature Conservation Committee (JNCC); [POL-022] 30×30 Technical Working Group; [LEG-004] Environment Act 2021; JNCC UK Biodiversity Indicators; UN Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) / Kunming-Montreal GBF; [POL-078] 30by30 on land in England; [POL-110] 30 by 30 in Scotland

Name: UN Convention to Combat Desertification
Key_Provisions: Only legally binding international framework addressing desertification and the effects of drought. Promotes sustainable land management, Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) commitment (Target 15.3 SDG). Covers drylands in 100+ countries. Joint work programme with UNFCCC and CBD (Rio Conventions). Adopted a 2030 strategic framework; LDN target adopted by 127 countries.
UK_Links: Defra 25 Year Environment Plan; [POL-009] Land Use Framework (LUF) 2025; [POL-010] England Peat Action Plan 2021

Name: Ramsar Convention on Wetlands
Key_Provisions: Intergovernmental treaty providing framework for conservation and wise use of wetlands. Designates Wetlands of International Importance (Ramsar Sites). Parties commit to wise use of all wetlands, designate at least one Ramsar site, and cooperate on transboundary wetlands. 175 Ramsar sites in UK, Overseas Territories and Crown Dependencies. Strategic Plan 2016–2024. Links to CBD, CMS, and World Heritage Convention.
UK_Links: [ORG-005] Natural England; [ORG-014] NatureScot; [ORG-015] Natural Resources Wales (NRW); [ORG-004] Joint Nature Conservation Committee (JNCC); [POL-001] Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025

Name: Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species
Key_Provisions: Legally binding international agreement regulating international trade in specimens of wild animals and plants to prevent overexploitation. Three appendices with varying levels of protection. Requires import/export permits from national Management Authorities. COP meets every 3 years. APHA is UK CITES Management Authority. UK Scientific Authority is JNCC. Around 38,000 species covered.
UK_Ratification: Ratified 1976; APHA is UK Management Authority; JNCC is UK Scientific Authority
UK_Links: [ORG-020] Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA); [ORG-004] Joint Nature Conservation Committee (JNCC); [LEG-005] Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981 (as amended)

Name: Convention on Migratory Species (CMS / Bonn Convention)
Key_Provisions: Intergovernmental treaty under UNEP auspices for conservation of migratory animals across their migratory range. Appendix I (endangered): strict protection; Appendix II (unfavourable conservation status): encourage agreements. Has prompted several regional agreements including ASCOBANS (cetaceans), AEWA (waterbirds), EUROBATS (bats). JNCC provides scientific advice. Works alongside Ramsar, CBD.
UK_Links: [ORG-004] Joint Nature Conservation Committee (JNCC); [LEG-005] Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981 (as amended)

Name: Bern Convention on European Wildlife and Natural Habitats
Key_Provisions: Council of Europe treaty requiring strict protection of >500 plant and >1,000 animal species listed in appendices. Protects migratory birds and their habitats. Establishes Emerald Network (equivalent of EU Natura 2000 for non-EU countries). Post-Brexit UK remains party as independent contracting party.
UK_Ratification: Ratified 1982; UK continues as independent party post-Brexit
UK_Links: [LEG-005] Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981 (as amended); [LEG-007] Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2017; [ORG-005] Natural England; [ORG-014] NatureScot; [ORG-015] Natural Resources Wales (NRW)

Name: OSPAR Convention for the Protection of the Marine Environment of the North-East Atlantic
Key_Provisions: Legally binding treaty combining the Oslo (1972) and Paris (1974) Conventions. Covers all pollution sources affecting the North-East Atlantic. Five annexes: I (land-based), II (dumping), III (offshore), IV (radioactive substances), V (biodiversity and ecosystems, added 1998). Guided by precautionary and polluter-pays principles. North-East Atlantic Environment Strategy 2030 (NEAES 2030). Amended 2025 to enlarge maritime area.
UK_Ratification: Ratified 1998; Annex V and Appendix 3 ratified 2000
UK_Links: [LEG-011] Marine and Coastal Access Act 2009; [LEG-022] Marine Strategy Regulations 2010 (as amended); [ORG-008] Marine Management Organisation (MMO); [ORG-004] Joint Nature Conservation Committee (JNCC); [ORG-005] Natural England; [POL-028] UK Marine Strategy (UKMS) 2025 — Programme of Measures

Name: UN Convention on the Law of the Sea
Secretariat_Location: Kingston, Jamaica (International Seabed Authority / Division for Ocean Affairs, DOALOS)
Key_Provisions: Comprehensive international framework governing all aspects of ocean space including territorial sea, EEZ, continental shelf, high seas and the international seabed area. Part XII protects the marine environment. Provides legal basis for all marine governance. Parent treaty for BBNJ Agreement and key framework for OSPAR, IMO, ISA activities.
UK_Links: [LEG-011] Marine and Coastal Access Act 2009; [LEG-010] Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction Act 2026; [ORG-008] Marine Management Organisation (MMO)

Name: Agreement on Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ — 'High Seas Treaty')
Key_Provisions: Legally binding international agreement under UNCLOS on conservation and sustainable use of marine biological diversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction (ABNJ — the high seas). Four elements: marine genetic resources (ABS); area-based management tools (ABMTs) and marine protected areas; environmental impact assessments (EIAs); capacity building and technology transfer. Historic agreement for high seas governance.
Parent_Convention: [INT-L-014] UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS)
Status: Signed 2023; ratification phase (UK ratified via Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction Act 2026)
UK_Ratification: Ratified Feb 2026 via Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction Act 2026
UK_Links: [LEG-010] Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction Act 2026; [ORG-008] Marine Management Organisation (MMO); [ORG-004] Joint Nature Conservation Committee (JNCC)

Name: International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships
Key_Provisions: Main international convention covering prevention of pollution of the marine environment by ships. 6 annexes: oil; noxious liquid substances; harmful substances in packaged form; sewage; garbage; air pollution (Annex VI). Annex VI covers ship emission standards (SOx, NOx, CO2). IMO 2023 GHG Strategy targets net-zero shipping by 2050. UK MCA administers MARPOL compliance.
UK_Ratification: Party; Maritime and Coastguard Agency (MCA) administers
UK_Links: Shipping sector (Climate Act & Net Zero); [ORG-001] Defra (Dept for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs)

Name: Helsinki Convention (HELCOM) — Baltic Marine Environment Protection Convention
Key_Provisions: Legally binding convention for protection of the marine environment of the Baltic Sea area. Requires joint programmes and measures to reduce land-based, ship-source and airborne pollution. Works alongside OSPAR for North Sea. UK is not a HELCOM party but OSPAR cooperates with HELCOM. Included for completeness as key regional marine governance body.
UK_Ratification: UK is not a party (North Sea covered by OSPAR)
UK_Links: [LEG-011] Marine and Coastal Access Act 2009; [LEG-022] Marine Strategy Regulations 2010 (as amended)

Name: London Protocol (Protocol to the Convention on the Prevention of Marine Pollution by Dumping of Wastes)
Key_Provisions: Protocol to the London Convention (1972) on dumping of wastes at sea. Prohibits dumping except for listed materials (dredged material, sewage sludge, fish waste etc.). Amended in 2006 to allow sub-seabed CO2 storage under OSPAR framework. Amended in 2009 to allow marine geo-engineering research. IMO administers; Environment Agency acts as UK competent authority.
UK_Links: [LEG-011] Marine and Coastal Access Act 2009; [ORG-006] Environment Agency (EA)

Name: Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer
Key_Provisions: Legally binding treaty phasing out production and use of ozone-depleting substances (ODSs). Kigali Amendment (2016) extends phase-down of hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs — potent GHGs). One of the most successful international environmental agreements. UN Environment Programme administers. Directly relevant to F-gas indicators in UK climate monitoring.
UK_Links: F-gas emissions (Climate Act & Net Zero); Waste & F-gases sector indicators; [ORG-001] Defra

Name: UNCCD Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) Framework and Voluntary Targets
Key_Provisions: Nations can voluntarily set Land Degradation Neutrality targets under the UNCCD framework. LDN means no net loss of productive land and ecosystem services over time. UK has not formally set LDN targets but Environment Act 2021 targets and EIP 2025 align with LDN principles. Supports SDG Target 15.3. Closely linked to 30×30 commitments.
UK_Ratification: UK aligned but no formal LDN targets set
UK_Links: [POL-001] Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; [POL-009] Land Use Framework (LUF) 2025; [POL-010] England Peat Action Plan 2021

Name: UNESCO Convention Concerning the Protection of the World Cultural and Natural Heritage
Key_Provisions: Establishes framework for designating and protecting World Cultural and Natural Heritage sites. Natural World Heritage sites must have Outstanding Universal Value (OUV) based on natural criteria. UK has 7 natural/mixed World Heritage Sites (Jurassic Coast, Giant's Causeway etc.). Historic England and natural statutory bodies provide scientific input.
UK_Links: [ORG-005] Natural England; [ORG-014] NatureScot; [ORG-015] Natural Resources Wales (NRW); Historic England

Name: Aarhus Convention — UN/ECE Convention on Access to Information, Public Participation and Access to Justice in Environmental Matters
Key_Provisions: Establishes rights of access to environmental information, public participation in environmental decision-making, and access to justice in environmental matters. Important basis for UK environmental governance transparency. Post-Brexit UK continues as independent party. Aarhus Compliance Committee monitors compliance.
UK_Ratification: Ratified 2005; continues as independent party post-Brexit
UK_Links: [ORG-007] Office for Environmental Protection (OEP); [LEG-004] Environment Act 2021; [POL-111] Environmental Principles Policy Statement (EPPS)

Name: International Plant Protection Convention
Policy_Sector: Biosecurity | Nature & Biodiversity | Land Use & Agriculture
Secretariat_Location: Rome, Italy (IPPC Secretariat, hosted by FAO)
Key_Provisions: FAO multilateral treaty (revised text in force 2005) to prevent the international spread of plant pests and to promote appropriate phytosanitary measures. Sets the International Standards for Phytosanitary Measures (ISPMs, e.g. ISPM 15 on wood packaging). The reference standard-setting body for plant health under the WTO SPS Agreement. Operates through Regional Plant Protection Organizations (RPPOs) such as EPPO.
Parent_Convention: [INT-O-030] Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
UK_Links: [LEG-043] Plant Health Act 1967; [LEG-044] Plant Health (England) Order 2015; [LEG-044] Plant Health (Scotland) Order 2005; Plant Biosecurity Strategy for GB [POL-034]; [POL-033] Tree Health Resilience Strategy; [ORG-020] Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA); [ORG-009] Forestry Commission (FC)

Name: International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture
Secretariat_Location: Rome, Italy (Treaty Secretariat, hosted by FAO)
Key_Provisions: Binding FAO treaty, in harmony with the CBD, governing conservation and sustainable use of crop genetic diversity and fair sharing of benefits. Establishes a Multilateral System of Access and Benefit-sharing covering 64 major food and forage crops (Annex I) and recognises Farmers' Rights. Underpins agrobiodiversity and food-system resilience under climate change.
Parent_Convention: [INT-O-030] Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
UK_Links: [ORG-001] Defra; [ORG-019] Royal Botanic Gardens Kew (RBG Kew)
